title: Bioinformatics-Driven Identification of Common Host Key Molecular Signatures and Mechanisms Associated with Dengue-SARS-CoV-2 Coinfection for Disclosing Repurposable Unique Drug Molecules
content: Background and Objectives: Management of SARS-CoV-2 and dengue virus coinfections might be complicated compare to the management of either infection alone due to the conflicting of conventional diseases specific therapies, since a therapy of one disease may conflict with other disease. To reduce such complexities, so far, there is no a unique drug specifically approved to treat SARS‑CoV‑2–dengue virus co-infection as a combined condition. This study aimed to address this issue. Methods: Integrated bioinformatics web-tools and databases were employed to identify common host key molecular signatures and mechanisms associated with dengue-SARS-CoV-2 coinfection through combined RNA-seq profile analysis for prioritizing repurposable drug molecules. Results: At first, we disclosed dysregulated four common host key-genes (chKGs): CXCL10, IFIH1, STAT1 and IRF7 as the druggable key molecular signatures associated with the co-infection. Then two TFs-proteins (NFKB1 and RELA) and two miRNAs (has-let-7b-5p, and hsa-miR-34a-5p) were disclosed as the transcriptional and post- transcriptional regulators of chKGs, respectively. Some crucial biological pro-cesses, molecular processes, cellar components and KEGG-pathways of chKGs were identified that might be linked to the co-infection. Then chKGs-guided top-ranked four repurposable drug molecules (Naltrindole, Denifanstat, Proscillaridin and Imatinib) were suggested against the co-infection. Conclusion: The findings of this study might be useful resources to design an effective drug against the coinfection.
